en: The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest eagles in the world.
The sampaguita, scientifically known as Jasminum sambac, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
National hero Jose Rizal was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan, now known as Rizal Park, on December 30, 1896.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government, which makes the laws, is composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago by carving the mountains of the Cordilleras.
Filipino pediatrician Dr. Fe del Mundo invented an improvised bamboo incubator to provide affordable healthcare for newborns in rural areas.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño through a traditional two-steps-forward, one-step-back dance every January.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses characters representing syllables and was traditionally written on bamboo.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his masterpiece Spoliarium.
The narra tree, scientifically called Pterocarpus indicus, is the national tree of the Philippines and is highly valued for its durable wood.
